---
<!-- introthm-1: body_md -->
\label{main2-intro}
   Given a global field $K$, there exists a finite set of primes $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$, such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$, there is a short exact sequence
    \[ 0 \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(K), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \notin S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.\]
<!-- end introthm-1 -->
<!-- introthm-2: body_md -->
\label{torsionH2-intro}
    Given a global field $K$, with $r$ real embeddings, there exists a finite set of primes $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] $\operatorname{rk}(H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})), \mathbb{Z})=r$;
        \item[(ii)] $|H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}| = |K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|/{2^r}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end introthm-2 -->
<!-- introthm-3: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ be a ring of $S$-integers of a totally real abelian extension $K$, then there is $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$, such that for all $S \supseteq S_0$, we have, up to a power of $2$,
    \[
    |\zeta_K^S(-1)|=\frac{2^r \cdot |H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}|}{|w_2(K)|},
    \]
    where $r=[K: \mathbb{Q}]$.
<!-- end introthm-3 -->
<!-- introconj-1: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ be a ring of $S$-integers of a totally real extension $K$, then there is an $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$, such that for all $S \supseteq S_0$, we have, up to a power of $2$:
    \[
    |\zeta_K^S(-1)|=\frac{2^r \cdot |H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}|}{|w_2(K)|},
    \]
    where $r=[K: \mathbb{Q}]$.
<!-- end introconj-1 -->
<!-- introthm-4: body_md -->
If $2 \nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$ and $T$ is a set of primes of $K$ such that $T \supsetneq S $, then we have the following exact sequence: 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, T}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \in T\backslash S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end introthm-4 -->
<!-- introcor-1: body_md -->
If $2 \nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$, then there is a natural exact sequence: 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}),\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(K),\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \notin S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end introcor-1 -->
<!-- dfn-1: body_md -->
Let $K$ be a global field and let $S$ be a finite nonempty set of primes containing the set $S_\infty$ of all infinite primes. We define:
$$
\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\{a \in K^{\times} \text{ }| \text{ }v_{\mathfrak{p}}(a)\geq 0 \text{ for all } 
\mathfrak{p} \notin S \}. 
$$
A ring $A$ is said to be a \textit{Dedekind domain of arithmetic type}, or a \textit{ring of $S$-integers}, whenever $A=\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$. 
If $S = S_{\infty}$ and every prime in $S$ comes from an imaginary embedding $K \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we say that $A$ is \textit{totally imaginary}.
<!-- end dfn-1 -->
<!-- prp-1: body_md -->
{\cite[Theorem 3.1]{BBT2025-2}}\label{H1CHAR0}
                                                                                                                  
Suppose ${\rm char}(K) = 0$ and $A = \mathcal{O}_{K,S}$. Then
\[
H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{q}\in S_2\backslash S} \mathbb{Z}/4 \oplus 
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{q}\in S_2'\backslash S} (\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus \mathbb{Z}/2) \oplus
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{q}\in S_3\backslash S} \mathbb{Z}/3.
\]
<!-- end prp-1 -->
<!-- prp-2: body_md -->
{\cite[Theorem 3.2]{BBT2025-2}}\label{H1CHAR>0}
                                                                                                                                                                                                           
Suppose $K$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ and $A = \mathcal{O}_{K,S}$. Then

\[
H_1({\rm SL}_2(A),\mathbb{Z}) \simeq \begin{cases}
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{q}\in S_2''\backslash S}(\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus \mathbb{Z}/2) &  \text{if $q=2$}\\
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{q}\in S_3''\backslash S} \mathbb{Z}/3  & \text{if $q=3$.}\\
0 & \text{if $q\geq 4$}
\end{cases}
\]
<!-- end prp-2 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
$2 \mid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$ if and only if there exists some prime $\mathfrak{p} \mid (2)$ such that $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=2$ and $\mathfrak{p} \notin S$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{2inS}
    We will be mostly dealing with the case where $2\nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$, i.e. when all primes $\mathfrak{p}$ over $2$, with $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=2$, lie on $S$. In view of this, consider the set: 
    \begin{align}
    \label{S_2}
        \mathcal{S}_2 = \begin{cases}
        S_2 \cup S_2', &\text{if ${\rm char}(K)=0$}\\
        S_2^{''}, &\text{if ${\rm char}(K)>0$}
    \end{cases}.
    \end{align}
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
{\cite[Theorem 3.6]{PIBT}}\label{Gg_0Glob}
                                                                                                                                         
    Let $A=\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ and let $(0) \neq \mathfrak{p} \in {\rm Spec}(A)$.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [(i)] If $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})| \geq 4$, then
        \[
        H_1(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^\times \oplus H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}).
        \]
        \item [(ii)] If $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=3$, then
        \[
        H_1(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})\simeq \kappa(\mathfrak{p}) \oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^\times \oplus H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}).  
        \]
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{amalg}
Let $A=\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a nonzero prime ideal of $A$. Then
\[
{\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, S\cup \{\mathfrak{p}\}}) \simeq {\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}) \ast_{\Gamma_0(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}, \mathfrak{p})} {\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}).
\]
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
See \cite[p. 80, Example b)]{serre1980}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{pgroupiso}
    Let $k$ be any finite field of characteristic $p$ and let $M$ be an ${\rm SL}_2(k)$-module. Then, for all $i \geq 1$, the natural inclusion $B(k) \hookrightarrow {\rm SL}_2(k)$ induces an isomorphism
    \[
    H_i(B(k), M)_{(p)} \simeq H_i({\rm SL}_2(k), M)_{(p)}.
    \]
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See \cite[Corollary 3.10.2]{h2013}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
Since $B(k)$ and ${\rm SL}_2(k)$ are finite groups, their homologies $H_i(B(k), M)$ and $H_i({\rm SL}_2(k), M)$ are also finite \cite[Corollary 10.2, \S 10, Chap. III]{brown1994}.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{Lambda(G)}
    Let $\Lambda(G)$ be the cokernel of the natural map $H_2(H, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2(G, \mathbb{Z})$, i.e. the sequence 
    \[
    H_2(H, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \Lambda(G)\rightarrow 0
    \]
    is exact. Then $\Lambda(G)$ fits into the exact sequence
    \[
    0 \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{1,1} \rightarrow \Lambda(G) \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{2,0} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
The spectral sequence gives the filtration 
    \[
    0 = F_{-1}H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq F_0H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \subseteq F_2H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})= H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}).
    \]
    A careful analysis of this spectral sequence gives the following short exact sequences:
    \[
    0 \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{0,2} \rightarrow F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{1,1} \rightarrow 0
    \]
    and 
    \[
    0 \rightarrow F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{2,0} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    Moreover, we also obtain the surjective edge map:
    \[
    \lambda: H_2(H, \mathbb{Z}) \twoheadrightarrow H_2(H, \mathbb{Z})_{G/H} \simeq E^2_{0,2} \twoheadrightarrow E^{\infty}_{0,2} \simeq F_0H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}).
    \]
    Let $\gamma$ be the following composition
    \[
     H_2(H,\mathbb{Z}) \overset{\lambda}{\twoheadrightarrow} F_0H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \hookrightarrow H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}).
    \]
    Then $\Lambda(G) = {\rm coker} \ \gamma$. Thus, we then have the exact sequence
    \[
    H_2(H, \mathbb{Z}) \overset{\gamma}{\rightarrow} H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \Lambda(G) \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    Now, let $\beta$ be the composition
    \[
    H_2(H,\mathbb{Z}) \overset{\lambda}{\twoheadrightarrow} F_0H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \hookrightarrow F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}).
    \]
    Then we have the following commutative diagram with exact rows:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
    & H_2(H, \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r, "\gamma"]\ar[d, "\beta"]& H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]\ar[d, equal]& \Lambda(G) 
    \ar[r] \ar[d, "\alpha"]& 0\\
    0 \ar[r] & F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]& H_2(G, \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]& E^{\infty}_{2,0} \ar[r]& 0,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the map $\alpha$ is surjective and is induced as follows:
    \[
    \Lambda(G) \simeq \frac{H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})}{\rm im \ \gamma} = \frac{H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})}{F_0H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})} \twoheadrightarrow \frac{H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})}{F_1H_2(G,\mathbb{Z})} \simeq E^{\infty}_{2,0}.
    \]
    By applying the Snake lemma to the above diagram, we get $\rm ker \ \alpha = \rm coker \ \beta$. But $\textrm{coker} \ \beta = E^{\infty}_{1,1}$. Putting all these together, we obtain the required short exact sequence:
    \[
    0 \rightarrow E^{\infty}_{1,1} \rightarrow \Lambda(G) \overset{\alpha}{\rightarrow} E^{\infty}_{2,0} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- prp-3: body_md -->
\label{surj}
                                                                                                                                                                         
   Let $A=\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $A$ such that $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|\neq 2$. Then, the natural maps 
    \[
    i_{1\ast}: H_2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}) \ \text{ and } \ i_{2\ast}: H_2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z})
    \]
    are surjective.
<!-- end prp-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
We will show that $i_{1\ast}$ is surjective and, using analogous arguments, one can conclude the same for $i_{2\ast}$. For this, we split the proof in two cases: when $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})| \neq 3$ and when $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})| = 3$. 

     \vspace{0.3cm}
     (i) $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|\neq 3$: 
     \vspace{0.3cm}

     Consider the following commutative diagram with exact rows: 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
1 \ar[r] & \Gamma(A,\mathfrak{p}) \ar[r]\ar[d, equal]& \Gamma_0(A,\mathfrak{p}) \ar[r]\ar[d, "i_1"]& {\rm B}(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})) 
\ar[r] \ar[d, hook]& 1\\
1 \ar[r] & \Gamma(A,\mathfrak{p}) \ar[r]& {\rm SL}_2(A) \ar[r]& {\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})) \ar[r]& 1.
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}

From the top exact sequence we obtain a spectral sequence on the second page: 
\[
E_{i,j}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}))=H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}), H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})) \implies H_{i+j}(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}),
\]
while the bottom one gives us: 
\[
E_{i,j}^2({\rm SL}_2(A))=H_i({\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})) \implies H_{i+j}({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}).
\]
The image of the edge morphisms: $E_{0, j}^{\infty}(H) \rightarrow H_j(H,\mathbb{Z})$, coincides with the image of the maps $H_j(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_j(H, \mathbb{Z})$, for $H\in \{\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}), {\rm SL}_2(A)\}$. Hence, by analysis on the the $E^\infty$-terms of degree $2$ in the extension, we obtain a commutative digram of the form: 
     \begin{equation}
\begin{tikzcd}
\label{diag}
 H_2(\Gamma(A,\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]\ar[d, equal]& H_2(\Gamma_0(A,\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]\ar[d, "i_{1\ast}"]& \Lambda(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p})) 
\ar[r] \ar[d]& 0\\
H_2(\Gamma(A,\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]& H_2({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}) \ar[r]& \Lambda({\rm SL}_2(A)) \ar[r]& 0,
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda(H)$ is a group fitting into the exact sequence: 
\begin{equation}
\label{exactlamb}
0 \rightarrow  E_{1,1}^\infty(H) \rightarrow \Lambda(H) \rightarrow E_{2,0}^\infty(H) \rightarrow 0
\end{equation}
(see Lemma \ref{Lambda(G)}). By diagram chasing, it is enough to prove that the map $\Lambda(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p})) \rightarrow \Lambda({\rm SL}_2(A))$ is surjective. 
                                                                                   
By \cite[Lemma 2.9]{PIBT}, we have that:
\[
H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq G \oplus H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z}),
\]
where $G$ is a $p$-group.  By Propositions \ref{H1CHAR0} and \ref{H1CHAR>0}, $|H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z})| = 2^k3^s$, for some $k, s \in \mathbb{Z}$. If ${\rm char}(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})) \neq 2$, the same propositions give $H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)} =G$. Otherwise, when ${\rm char}(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}))=2$, we have $H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)}=G \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/4)^{S_2} \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/2 \oplus \mathbb{Z}/2)^{S_2'}$. Either way, we may write $H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})=\mathcal{K} \oplus \mathcal{G}$, where $\mathcal{K}=H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)}$.

Now, 
\begin{align*}
E_{i, 1}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}))=&H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}), H_1(\Gamma(A, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})) \simeq H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K} \oplus \mathcal{G)}\\
&\simeq H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K}) \oplus H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{G}).   
\end{align*}

Once $B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}))$ acts trivially on $H_1({\rm SL}_2(A), \mathbb{Z})$, it also acts trivially on $\mathcal{K}$. Therefore, by Universal Coefficient-Theorem, 
\begin{align*}
    H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K}) &\simeq H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z}) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathcal{K},\\
    H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{G}) &\simeq H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z}) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathcal{G}.
\end{align*}
By \cite[Corollary 3.10 (2)]{h2013}, we have that $H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z}) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathcal{G}\simeq 0$ for $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})| \neq 2, 3$. This implies that $E_{i,1}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})) \simeq H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K})=H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K})_{(p)}$ and by similar arguments we can show that $E_{i, 1}^2 ({\rm SL}_2(A)) \simeq H_i({\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathcal{K})_{(p)}$. As a consequence, Lemma~\ref{pgroupiso} ensures that
\[
E_{i,0}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})) \simeq E_{i,0}^2({\rm SL}_2(A)). 
\]
Evoking Lemma \ref{pgroupiso} again we obtain: 
\[
E_{i,0}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})) =H_i(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)} \simeq H_i({\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)}=E_{i, 0}^2({\rm SL}_2(A)). 
\]
On the other hand, since $E_{1, 1}^\infty=\operatorname{ker}(d_{1,1}^2: E_{3,0}^2 \rightarrow E_{1, 1}^2)$, and $E_{i, j}^2(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})) \simeq  E_{i, j}^2({\rm SL}_2(A))$ for $i \in \{1, 3\}$ and $j \in \{0, 1\}$, we have 
\[
E_{1,1}^\infty ({\rm SL}_2(A)) \simeq E_{1, 1}^\infty(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})).
\]
Moreover, $E_{2,0}^\infty=\ker(d_{2,0}^2: E_{2,0}^2 \rightarrow E_{0,1}^2)$ and, by the direct computations from \cite[$\S$ 3]{h2013}, we get: 
\[
H_2(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z})=H_2(B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)}\simeq H_2({\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})_{(p)}=H_2({\rm SL}_2(\kappa(\mathfrak{p})), \mathbb{Z}),
\]
so 
\[
E_{2,0}^\infty({\rm SL}_2(A)) \simeq E_{2,0}^{\infty} (\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p})). 
\]

By the sequence (\ref{exactlamb}), we obtain $\Lambda({\rm SL}_2(A))\simeq \Lambda(\Gamma_0(A, \mathfrak{p}))$. Now, diagram chasing applied on diagram (\ref{diag}) concludes the proof for this case.
\vspace{0.3cm}

(ii) $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=3$: 
\vspace{0.3cm}

In this case $B(\kappa(\mathfrak{p}))=\mathbb{F}_3$, so the proof can be obtained as in \cite[Theorem 5.2]{BBT2025-1}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{OK,S-OKS,P}
                                                                                                                                                                   
    Given a ring of $S$-integers $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ and a prime $\mathfrak{p} \in {\rm Spec}(\mathcal{O}_{K}) \backslash S$ such that $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})| \geq 3$, we have an exact sequence:
       \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup \{{\mathfrak{p}}\}}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^\times \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
We split the proof in two cases: when $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|> 3$ and when $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=3$. 
    \vspace{0.3cm}

    (i) $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|> 3$: 
    \vspace{0.3cm}
    
    By Propositions \ref{H1CHAR0} and \ref{H1CHAR>0}, $H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup\{\mathfrak{p}\}}), \mathbb{Z})\simeq H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})$. Combining with Proposition \ref{surj}, the Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence boils down to (integral coefficients are omitted):
    \[
        H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup\{\mathfrak{p}\}})) \rightarrow H_1(\Gamma_0(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}, \mathfrak{p})) \rightarrow H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})) \rightarrow 0.
    \]
     Now, from Theorem \ref{Gg_0Glob} (i), $H_1(\Gamma_0(\mathcal{O}_{K, S}, \mathfrak{p}), \mathbb{Z})\simeq H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times}$. Thus, replacing it in the above exact sequence, we get the required one:
    \[
       H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup \{{\mathfrak{p}}\}}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]

    (ii) $|\kappa(\mathfrak{p})|=3$: 
    \vspace{0.3cm}
    
    The proof follows in a similar vein. Propositions \ref{H1CHAR0} and \ref{H1CHAR>0} give the isomorphism $H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup \{\mathfrak{p}\}}), \mathbb{Z})\simeq H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})\oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p})$. Applying Proposition \ref{surj}, we obtain (integral coefficients again omitted):
    \[
            H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup\{\mathfrak{p}\}})) \rightarrow H_1(\Gamma_0(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}, \mathfrak{p})) 
      \rightarrow H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}))\oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p}) \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    
    Finally, Theorem \ref{Gg_0Glob} (ii) gives $H_1(\Gamma_0(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}, \mathfrak{p}),\mathbb{Z})\simeq H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, S}), \mathbb{Z})\oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p}) \oplus \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^\times$. Replacing it in the above exact sequence we get:
    \[
       H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S\cup \{{\mathfrak{p}}\}}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{Main} 
    If $2 \nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$ and $T$ is a set of primes of $K$ such that $T \supsetneq S $, then we have the following exact sequence: 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, T}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \in T\backslash S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
We proceed by induction on $|T \backslash S|$. The base case $|T \backslash S|=1$ is Lemma \ref{OK,S-OKS,P}. Now, let $|T \backslash S|>1$. Given $\mathfrak{q} \in T\backslash S$, we consider $T'=T \backslash \{\mathfrak{q}\}$. By Lemma \ref{OK,S-OKS,P}, we obtain an exact sequence: 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, T'}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,T}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \kappa(\mathfrak{q})^\times \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    Since $|T' \backslash S|< |T \backslash S|$, the induction hypothesis yields an exact sequence:
    \[
     H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \overset{\gamma}{\rightarrow} H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K, T^\prime}), \mathbb{Z}) \overset{\delta_{T^{\prime}}}{\rightarrow} \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \in T^\prime\backslash S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]    
    Now, by applying the Snake lemma to the following commutative diagram with exact rows:
    \[
\begin{tikzcd}
    & \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,T'}), \mathbb{Z}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "\delta_{T'}" , two heads] 
    & \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,T}), \mathbb{Z}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "\delta_T"] 
    & k(\mathfrak{q})^\times \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "\mathrm{id}"] 
    & 0 \\
  0 \arrow[r] 
    & \displaystyle\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p}\in T'\backslash S} k(\mathfrak{p})^\times \arrow[r] 
    & \displaystyle\bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p}\in T \backslash S} k(\mathfrak{p})^\times \arrow[r] 
    & k(\mathfrak{q})^\times \arrow[r] 
    & 0,
\end{tikzcd}
\]  
we get that $\delta_T$ and $(\ker \delta_{T^{\prime}} \rightarrow \ker \delta_{T})$ are surjective. Since $\ker \delta_{T^{\prime}} = {\rm im} \gamma$, $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})$ surjects onto $\ker \delta_{T}$, from which the result follows.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
This exact sequence cannot be obtained in general without the hypothesis of all inert primes over $2$ lying on $S$. For this, see Remark \ref{Sharpness} in next section.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{OKS_OKK}
   If $2 \nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$, then there is a natural exact sequence: 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}),\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(K),\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \notin S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Since $K = \underset{S\subset T}{\rm{colim \ }} \mathcal{O}_{K,T}$, the result follows immediately from Theorem \ref{Main} by taking colimits (here, the functor $\rm colim$ is just union and is right exact).
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- dfn-2: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. The second Steinberg group of $A$, $\operatorname{St}_2(A)$, is defined as the free group generated by the letters $x_{ij}(\lambda), \lambda \in A, 1 \leq i \neq j \leq 2$, and $w_{ij}(u):=x_{ij}(u)x_{ji}(-u)x_{ij}(u)$, with $u \in A^\times$, subject to the following relations:     
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [(i)] $x_{ij}(s)x_{ij}(t)=x_{ij}(s+t)$;
        \item [(ii)] $w_{ij}(u)x_{ij}(t)w_{ij}(-u)=x_{ji}(-u^{-2}t)$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end dfn-2 -->
<!-- dfn-3: body_md -->
The unstable $K_2$-group of degree 2 of $A$, denoted by $K_2(2, A)$, is defined to be the kernel of $\phi$.
<!-- end dfn-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
{\cite{mat1969, moore1968}}\label{matso1}
    Let $F$ be an infinite field.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [(i)] The exact sequence
    \[
    1 \rightarrow K_2(2, F) \rightarrow {\rm St}(2, F) \rightarrow {\rm SL}_2(F) \rightarrow 1
    \]
    is a universal central extension of the group ${\rm SL}_2(F)$. In particular, 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(F), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq K_2(2, F).
    \]
    \item [(ii)] The group $K_2(2, F)$ is the free group generated by symbols $c(u,v)$, with $u, v \in K^\times$, subject to the following relations: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [(a)] $c(u,v)=1$, whenever $u=1$ or $v=1$;
        \item [(b)] $c(u, v)=c(u^{-1}, v)$;
        \item [(c)] $c(u, vw)c(v, w)=c(uv, w) c(u, v)$, with $w\in K^\times$;
        \item [(d)] $c(u,v) = c(u, -uv)$;
        \item [(e)] $c(u, v)=c(u, (1-u)v)$, with $u\neq 1$. 
    \end{itemize}
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
{\cite[$\S$ 12]{milnor1971}} \label{matso2}
    Let $F$ be a field. Then $K_2(F)$ is isomorphic to the free group generated by symbols $\{x, y\}, x, y \in F^\times$, subject to the following relations: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [(i)] $\{x, 1-x\}=1, x \neq 1$;
        \item [(ii)] $\{x_1x_2,y\}=\{x_1, y\}\{x_2, y\}$; 
        \item [(iii)] $\{x, y_1y_2\}=\{x, y_1\}\{x, y_2\}$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{K2(2K)K2(K)}
    For any field $F$, the following homomorphism of groups is surjective: 
    \begin{align*}
    \psi: K_2(2, F) \rightarrow K_2(F), \ \text{ with } \ c(u,v) \mapsto \{u,v\}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- exa-1: body_md -->
\label{Z1/m}
    For the case of rational numbers, $K_2^{MW}(\mathbb{Q})$ is known to be $\mathbb{Z} \oplus \underset{p \ \text{prime}}{\bigoplus} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ \cite[Proposition 2.5]{kolderup22}. Using this information in the exact sequence of Corollary \ref{OKS_OKK} for $\mathcal{O}_{K,S} = \mathbb{Z}[1/2n]$, where $n$ is a positive odd integer, we have                                                                                                                          
    \begin{equation}\label{seq-Q}
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/2n],\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}),\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{p \nmid n\text{, prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times} \rightarrow 0,
    \end{equation}
    which becomes
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/2n],\mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \mathbb{Z} \oplus \bigoplus_{p \ \text{prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times} \rightarrow \bigoplus_{p \nmid n\text{, prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times} \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    Note that, by \cite[Theorem 6.8]{BBT2025-1},
    \[H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/2n], \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathbb{Z} \oplus \bigoplus_{p \mid n\text{, prime}}\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}.\]
    In this case, sequence \ref{seq-Q} is actually short exact, motivating us to ask in what other cases this is true. As we will see in the next subsection, this question is associated to the study of the group $\tilde{K}_2(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, defined by Hutchinson \cite[$\S$ 6]{h2016}.
<!-- end exa-1 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
With our finds and knowing that $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}), \mathbb{Z})$ is an abelian group of rank $1$ \cite[Remark 6.7]{h2016}, we can deduce that $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq  \mathbb{Z} \oplus \underset{p \ \text{prime}}{\bigoplus} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$, recovering Kolderup's description of $K_2^{MW}(\mathbb{Q})$ \cite[Proposition 2.5]{kolderup22}. Indeed, we can write $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Q}),\mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathbb{Z} \oplus H$, for some abelian group $H$ formed by a direct sum of divisible and/or reduced groups \cite[Chap. IV]{fuchs1970}. Thus, for $n=1$, sequence \ref{seq-Q} is short exact:
    \[
    0 \rightarrow \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z} \oplus H \rightarrow \bigoplus_{p \text{ prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times} \rightarrow 0,
    \]
    and hence $\frac{\mathbb{Z} \oplus H}{\mathbb{Z}} \simeq \bigoplus_{p \text{ prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$, i.e. $H \simeq \bigoplus_{p \text{ prime}} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- dfn-4: body_md -->
The group $\tilde{K}_2(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ is the kernel of the map $T_S$.
<!-- end dfn-4 -->
<!-- dfn-5: body_md -->
We define $K_2(K)_+$ as the kernel of the map $T_{\Omega}$, which is the so called \textit{group of totally positive elements of} $K_2(K)$. Moreover, we define $K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})_+$ as the intersection $K_2(K)_+ \cap K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$.
<!-- end dfn-5 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\cite[Lemma 6.3]{h2016}
\label{K2tilde}
                                                                                           
    $\tilde{K_2}(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S}) \simeq K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})_+\oplus \ \mathbb{Z}^r$,
    where $r$ denotes the number of real embeddings of $K$.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- exa-2: body_md -->
\cite[Example 6.2]{h2016}
\label{irredk2z}
    If $K=\mathbb{Q}$ and $m >1$ is an integer, then $\tilde{K_2}(2, \mathbb{Z}[1/m])\simeq \mathbb{Z} \oplus \bigoplus_{p\mid m} \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$.
<!-- end exa-2 -->
<!-- exa-3: body_md -->
\cite[Lemma 6.1]{h2016}
\label{K2Ima1}
    If $K$ is a global field of positive characteristic or a totally imaginary number field, then 
    $\tilde{K_2}(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S}) \simeq K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$.
<!-- end exa-3 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 6.10]{h2016}\label{Main2}
   Given a global field $K$, there exists a finite set of primes $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$, 
    \[
    H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \tilde{K_2}(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S}).
    \]
    Hence, there is a short exact sequence
    \[ 0 \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H_2({\rm SL}_2(K), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \bigoplus_{\mathfrak{p} \notin S} \kappa(\mathfrak{p})^{\times} \rightarrow 0.\]
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
In Hutchinson's original formulation, he states that there exists a set of primes $S_0$ such that $\mathcal{O}_{K,S_0}$ contains a unit $\lambda$ with $\lambda^2 -1$ unit, and satisfies the isomorphism with $\tilde{K}_2(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S_0})$. We believe that, in general, we can find a set of primes $S_0$ satisfying weaker conditions for which $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \tilde{K}_2(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, for all $S \supseteq S_0$ (for instance, see Example \ref{Z1/m}).
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
\label{Sharpness}
     The isomorphism between $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})$ and $\tilde{K}_2(2, \mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ is not always true. For example, by \cite{an1998}, we have $H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/37]),\mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathbb{Z}^6 \oplus \mathbb{Z}/6$. But, according to Example \ref{irredk2z}, $\tilde{K_2}(2, \mathbb{Z}[1/37])\simeq \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{F}_{37}^\times$. In this case, $2 \mid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/37]),\mathbb{Z})| = 12$, suggesting that the hypothesis of $2 \nmid |H_1({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})|$ (or $S \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$) is needed.
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{torsionH_2}
    Given a global field $K$, with $r$ real embeddings, there exists a finite set of primes $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] $\operatorname{rk}(H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})), \mathbb{Z})=r$;
        \item[(ii)] $|H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}| = |K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|/{2^r}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Let $S_0$ be the set of primes given by Theorem \ref{Main2}. From Lemma \ref{K2tilde}, we know that 
    \[ H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z}) \simeq K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})_+ \oplus \mathbb{Z}^r.\]
    Since $K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})/K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})^{+} \simeq (\mathbb{F}_2)^r$ (see (\ref{seq-k2+})), we have that 
    \[|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})_+| = \frac{|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|}{2^r}.\]
    We conclude that the rank of the second homology of ${\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ is $r$ and the size of the torsion is $|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|/2^r$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{coh-torsion}
    Let $G$ be a group such that $H_n(G, \mathbb{Z})$ and $H_{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z})$ are finitely generated. Then, $H^{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z})$ is also finitely generated and
    \[ \operatorname{rk}H_{n +1}(G, \mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{rk} H^{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z}) \ \ \text{ and } \ \ H_n(G, \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}} \simeq H^{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}.\]
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The Universal Coefficients Theorem for cohomology \cite[Theorem 12.11]{rotman1988} gives the following split short exact sequence:
    \[
    0 \rightarrow {\rm Ext}_{\mathbb{Z}}^1(H_n(G, \mathbb{Z}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow H^{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow {\rm Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}}(H_{n+1}(G,\mathbb{Z}), \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow 0.
    \]
    Recall some well-known properties \cite{rotman2008}: the functors $\rm Ext_{\mathbb{Z}}^1( -, \mathbb{Z})$ and $\rm Hom_{\mathbb{Z}}(-, \mathbb{Z})$ commute with direct sums of finitely many summands; $\rm Ext_{\mathbb{Z}}^1(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$; $\rm Hom_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}) \simeq \mathbb{Z}$; $\rm Ext_{\mathbb{Z}}^1(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z})$ and $\rm Hom_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z})$ are trivial.

    By applying these properties, the above short exact sequence boils down to
    \[
    0 \rightarrow H_n(G, \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}} \rightarrow H^{n+1}(G, \mathbb{Z}) \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}^{\operatorname{rk}H_{n +1}(G, \mathbb{Z})} \rightarrow 0,
    \]
    and so the result follows by the splitting.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{H2structCoh}
    Given a global field $K$, with $r$ real embeddings, there exists a finite set of primes $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$, 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] $\operatorname{rk}(H^2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})), \mathbb{Z})=r$;
        \item[(ii)] $|H^3({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}| = |K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|/{2^r}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
{\cite{klingen1962}}
    Let $m$ be a negative integer. Then $\zeta_K(m) \in \mathbb{Q}.$
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- conj-1: body_md -->
\label{BTC}
    Let $K$ be a totally real number field. Then, up to a power of $2$,
     \[
     |\zeta_K(-1)|=\frac{|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K})|}{|w_2(K)|},
     \] 
     where  $w_2(K)$ be the number of roots of unity on $K(\sqrt{K})$.
<!-- end conj-1 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{BTT}
Let $A=\mathcal{O}_K$ be the ring of integers of a totally real abelian extension. Then
 \[
|\zeta_K(-1)|=\frac{|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K})|}{|w_2(K)|}.
\]
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- conj-2: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ be a ring of $S$-integers. Then, up to a power of $2$, 
    \[
    |\zeta_K^{S}(-1)|= \frac{|K_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})|}{|w_2(K)|}.
    \]
<!-- end conj-2 -->
<!-- conj-3: body_md -->
\label{BThomconj}
    Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ be a ring of $S$-integers of a totally real extension $K$ with $[K: \mathbb{Q}] = r$. Then, there is an $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$, we have, up to a power of $2$,
    \[
    |\zeta_K^S(-1)|=\frac{2^r \cdot |H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}|}{|w_2(K)|}.
    \]
<!-- end conj-3 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{BThomthm}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    Let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ be a ring of $S$-integers of a totally real extension $K$ with $[K: \mathbb{Q}] = r$. Then, there is an $S_0 \supseteq \mathcal{S}_2$ such that, for all $S \supseteq S_0$, we have, up to a power of $2$,
    \[
    |\zeta_K^S(-1)|=\frac{2^r \cdot |H_2({\rm SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S}), \mathbb{Z})_{\operatorname{tor}}|}{|w_2(K)|}.
    \]
<!-- end thm-10 -->
